response: The cobalt blue light slit-lamp biomicroscopy method (SLBM) can be used to measure mesopic pupil size, but it has some limitations. Although the method is quite repeatable, it tends to underestimate mesopic pupil size and has a wide range of agreement with other methods, such as the CIP. Additionally, the SLBM shows low sensitivity in detecting pupils larger than 6 mm, which may be misleading when planning anterior segment surgery. However, previous grading-consensus training strategies may increase interrater reproducibility, and compensation for the systematic underestimation could improve the accuracy of the SLBM. Therefore, while the SLBM can be used to measure mesopic pupil size, its results should be interpreted with caution and considered in conjunction with other methods to ensure accurate assessments.
